references.text: Balak sent messengers to summon Bileam to curse Israel, but God refused to let Bileam curse them.
Bileam blessed Israel instead of cursing them, because the Lord put words in his mouth.
Balak became angry with Bileam because he blessed Israel three times instead of cursing them.
Joshua reminds the people that Balak sent messengers to summon Bileam, but the Lord would not listen to him and turned the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah refers to how Bileam was hired to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
Micah reminds the people of what Balak planned and how Bileam answered, so that they may know the Lord's righteous deeds.
The Lord loved Israel and kept the oath he had sworn to their ancestors, which explains why He turned the curse into a blessing.
All things work together for good for those who love God, just as God turned the curse into a blessing because He loved Israel.
